edges.description: Without enough cytoplasmic laforin and malin, glycogen is built with overlong strands and becomes insoluble polyglucosan that aggregates into Lafora bodies.

edges.description: Insoluble polyglucosan aggregates accumulate intracellularly as periodic acid-Schiff-positive Lafora bodies detectable on skeletal muscle biopsy.
In Lafora disease models, Lafora body inclusions drive neurodegeneration; the same step is assumed here.
intermediate_mechanisms: glycogen-driven neuroinflammation, autophagy impairment and synaptic dysfunction

edges.description: Early dysarthria is a presenting feature.
Ataxia is a presenting feature in the founding family.
A complicated spastic paraplegia-like presentation was seen in the Iranian family.
Progressive neurodegeneration can involve four-limb spastic weakness in occasional patients.
Generalized EEG discharges were recorded without clinical seizures in the Iranian family.
Clinical seizures arise during the childhood-onset progressive myoclonus epilepsy course.
Progressive cognitive decline develops over the childhood-to-adulthood disease course.
Hyperreflexia accompanies spasticity during the protracted neurodegenerative course.
Protracted neurodegeneration into adulthood manifests with psychosis and outbursts of prolonged agitation and screaming.
Confusion develops during the protracted adult stage of progressive neurodegeneration.
Mutism develops in advanced stages as speech and cognitive function deteriorate into adulthood.

nodes.description: Progressive neurological decline giving a protracted progressive myoclonus epilepsy course with childhood-onset dysarthria, myoclonus, ataxia, seizures, and cognitive decline, followed in adulthood by behavioral/psychotic outbursts, spasticity and spastic tetraparesis, hyperreflexia, confusion, and mutism, alongside a complicated spastic paraplegia-like presentation in the Iranian family.

evidence.snippet: The subsequent course is a typical progressive myoclonus epilepsy, though much more protracted than any infantile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis, or Lafora disease, patients living into the fourth decade.

nodes.description: Laforin (glycogen phosphatase) and malin (E3 ubiquitin ligase) act in the cytoplasm to regulate glycogen construction. Excess nuclear sequestration by mutant PRDM8 leaves an effective cytoplasmic deficiency of both enzymes, the same functional deficit that EPM2A or NHLRC1 loss produces in classic Lafora disease.
nodes.id: Nuclear sequestration of laforin and malin

evidence.snippet: We show that the PRDM8 protein interacts with laforin and malin and causes translocation of the two proteins to the nucleus.
The mutation, c.781T>C (Phe261Leu), is in a gene of unknown function, PRDM8.

nodes.description: The founding variant, PRDM8 c.781T>C (p.Phe261Leu), alters a protein that normally interacts with laforin and malin and translocates them to the nucleus. The mutant protein sequesters both enzymes in the nucleus to an excessive degree, which the authors interpret as a gain of function.

nodes.description: Insoluble polyglucosan aggregates into Lafora bodies, which were found on pathology in the founding family; while the founding abstract (PMID:22961547) does not name the biopsied tissue, Orphanet (ORPHA:324290) specifies skeletal muscle biopsy showing periodic acid-Schiff-positive inclusions. Skin biopsies in both families were negative for Lafora bodies, so skin biopsy does not exclude the disease. The neuron cell type is inferred from the neurological presentation and from classic Lafora disease.

nodes.description: No PRDM8-specific or disease-modifying therapy is reported. Myoclonus and seizures are treated as in other progressive myoclonus epilepsies, with valproic acid as the drug of choice and levetiracetam or clonazepam as the first add-on. This guidance covers the progressive myoclonus epilepsies as a group and has not been studied in this disease.
